nodes.label: Task K4 Report — undefined-length SQ/items and encapsulated fragments stream natively; tail-fallback deleted; consume() live (commits 4b3968d+dc9da76)
Per-subtree EventBuffer for undefined-length SQ length backfill
nodes.rationale: The brief preferred deleting event buffering entirely, but buffered fromPart10 emits startSequence/startItem with the parser's COMPUTED content span (not on-wire 0xFFFFFFFF), which is unknown until the closing delimiter — and startSequence must precede its items. So defined-length SQ/items emit directly while undefined-length SQ/items buffer subtree events (lambdas with decoded values baked in) just long enough to backfill the span, then flush. Bounded by metadata-sized subtrees (~1.9KB corpus max); pixel data is encapsulated, never SQ, so it streams unbuffered. The K3 tail-fallback EventBuffer role (atomicity) was deleted along with TailFallbackSignal/triggerTailFallback/walkBodyTail.

nodes.label: Chunk release live — clearBuffers:true + consume() at top-level element boundaries
nodes.rationale: After every completed top-level element the stream calls consume(stream.offset), releasing fully-passed chunks (verified by a getBufferMemoryInfo smoke test: final retained totalSize < fileLen/2). Deflate and raw-dataset fallbacks never consume (they need full bytes until K5). Safe under D-E because every retained buffer is a fresh slice() copy. Granularity limit acknowledged: a single huge pixel-data element retains its bytes until it completes; the formal bounded-memory gate is K6.

nodes.label: Accepted stream-vs-buffered divergences (encapsulated startElement 0xFFFFFFFF; undefined-length text VRs throw loudly)
nodes.rationale: Two documented, test-pinned divergences: (1) emitEncapsulated emits startElement length as on-wire 0xFFFFFFFF instead of buffered's computed span — forced by fragment streaming, since the span is unknown until the closing delimiter and emitting startElement first is what lets fragments arrive before input completes; (2) undefined-length text VRs (UT/UC/UR, non-conformant per PS3.5) — buffered silently swallows the delimiter and trailing elements into a garbage string, the stream throws loudly (stream is BETTER). Both are gate-visible only through dedicated raw-event assertions.
